An inline destructor body gives the vtable and RTTI vague linkage, so they come out of every odr-using TU whatever the declaration position; declared-and-undefined makes the destructor the key function and confines all three to the one TU that defines it. That TU is src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD1Ev.cpp, which stays enrolled, and objisolate keeps its .text and discards its data.

TWO PROMOTED PRECEDENTS HAVE EXACTLY THIS SHAPE, and they were the model for the range above. ov074/daKuriKing_c and ov066/Eyerok are coined classes whose symbols.txt aliases only _ZTV (no _ZTS/_ZTI alias); both declare the destructor out of line and first, both hold D1/D0 out of the licensed run (daKuriKing_c 36 functions from 0x0211f154 with D1/D0 at 0x0211f000/0x0211f0a0; Eyerok 34 from 0x021184c0), and both are status:promoted and both carry _ZN7Vector3D1Ev as a compiler_only_output row -- daKuriKing_c's only one, while Eyerok carries a second, _ZN4Vec4D1Ev, the implicit destructor of the file-local shadow struct its ordinal 50 declares. The cost is two functions, not the class.

THE ROMDATA COST OF THE LEVER IS ZERO, measured rather than assumed, because the switch does not change what any ENROLLED source emits. tools/romdata_check.py reads src/, and src_tu/actors/d_a_spd.cpp is a shadow TU that is never in the build under either shape. With the inline body the vtable comes out of src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD1Ev.cpp by vague linkage; with the body removed it comes out of the same file as the key function's owner. Run over src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD1Ev.cpp, src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD0Ev.cpp and src/_ZN10Scuttlebug13OnYoshiTryEatEv.cpp, both shapes report an identical 9 data symbols: VERIFIED 4 (156 bytes), PARTIAL 3 (24 bytes), DIFFERS 0, UNNAMED 2. The two UNNAMED are _ZTI10Scuttlebug and _ZTS10Scuttlebug, which have no symbols.txt address to compare against and can never verify under any shape, since those names are not in the cartridge.

DESTRUCTOR SHARDS: the inline-body shape had left src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN10ScuttlebugD0Ev.cpp redefining a destructor the header already defined, so both failed to compile -- "object 'Scuttlebug::~Scuttlebug()' redefined" -- and the whole-tree build was red on this branch. No gate on the branch reported it, because linkcheck stopped at the object audit before mwldarm ran. Reverting the header to the declared-and-undefined form restores both shards to their original out-of-line definitions with no forcing scaffold at all, and both re-measure MATCH.
